units: <cite ref="Berakhot 47b">Ber. 47ᵇ</cite>, sq. <he>קטן פּוֹרֵחַ</he> a boy developing signs of puberty (before the usual age).

<cite ref="Mishnah Negaim 8:1">Neg. VIII, 1</cite> <he>הפורח מן הטמא טהור</he> a leprosy that ‘blossoms’ after the person has been declared unclean, is clean.
<cite ref="Mishnah Negaim 8:2">Ib. 2</cite> <he>פָּרְחָה בכולו</he> if it spread over the entire body.
Ib. VII, 5 עד שתִּפְרַח בכולו until it spreads over &c.; a. fr.—2) to fly, fly off; to swim.

IV, 68ᶜ</cite> top <he>הלוחות היו מבקשין לִפְרוֹחַ</he> the tablets wanted to fly (off Moses’ hands); <he>הכתב עצמו פ׳</he> only the letters flew off; <he>כיון שפ׳ הכתב וכ׳</he> when the letters had flown off, the tablets became too heavy for Moses’ hands.
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 18a:11">Ab. Zar. 18ᵃ</cite> (of a martyr dying on the pyre) <he>גוילין … פּוֹרְחוֹת</he> I see the sheets of the book of the Law burn, and the letters fly off.
<cite ref="Chagigah 15b">Ḥag. 15ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Sanhedrin 106b:11">Snh. 106ᵇ</cite> <he>מגדל הפורח באויר</he>, v. <cite ref="M00120"><he>מִגְדָּל</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Chagigah 1:8">Ḥag. I, 8</cite> <he>פּוֹרְחִין באויר</he>, v. <cite ref="E00495"><he>הֶיתֵּר</he></cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 93">Gen. R. s. 93</cite>, a. e. <he>פָּרְחָה נשמתן</he> their soul fled, i.e. they were shocked by surprise, fear &c.

senses.gloss: to place beyond due limits, to cause to protrude.
units: <cite ref="Bava Kamma 29b">B. Kam. 29ᵇ</cite>, sq. <he>לא שנו אלא</he> (<cite ref="B00000"><he>ב</he></cite>)<he>מַפְרִיחַ</he> this has been taught (that he is responsible for damage) only when he places the thorns on his ground so that they protrude into the public road, opp. <he>מצמצם</he> when he puts them exactly where his limits end.
<cite ref="Tosefta Bava Kamma 2:5">Tosef. ib. II, 5</cite> <he>המפריח גדירו … לרשות הרבים</he> he who causes his fence of thorns or stones to protrude into the public road.
